validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: independently confirmed by FIVE separate origins that agree with each other and predate/postdate GEM's own citation pool: (1) FERC's own Certificate Order, Columbia Gulf Transmission, LLC, 172 FERC P 61,260 (2020), Docket No. CP19-488-000, issued Sept 17, 2020 -- grants authorization to construct 3 new compressor stations (Shelburn/East Carroll Parish, Red Mountain/Catahoula Parish, Chicot/Evangeline Parish) plus modifications at the existing Alexandria Compressor Station (Rapides Parish), all in Louisiana, for 'the Louisiana XPress Project'; (2) the Federal Register's 2022-08-01 notice of request for extension of time (Columbia Gulf Transmission, LLC; Docket CP19-488-000) documents active, ongoing construction through 2022; (3) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset tracks this exact project (docket CP19-488) across every release from July 2019 through August 2026, consistently as a Columbia Gulf Transmission expansion, 493 MMcf/d, $472M, in-service 2022; (4) Natural Gas Intelligence's 2022 trade-press article on the extension-of-time filing, independently describing the same project, same docket, same compressor stations, same 493,000 Dth/d and 850,000 Dth/d figures; (5) TC Energy's own Louisiana XPress Project fact sheet (public PDF, content dated May 2022), which names and maps the same three new + one upgraded compressor stations and gives a construction/in-service timeline matching the regulatory record. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission expansion (compression-only capacity addition on an interstate natural gas transmission system regulated under NGA section 7(c)), not a gathering or distribution line -- confirmed by the FERC certificate itself. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 41-PID roster for this batch. Not a duplicate of P3188 (Columbia [Gulf] East Lateral Xpress Project, a separate FERC docket/project delivering to Plaquemines LNG rather than Sabine Pass) or P4448 (Columbia Gulf Mainline 100/200 Replacement Project, Docket CP19-193, a pipe-replacement project in Menifee/Montgomery Counties, Kentucky -- a different physical facility on the same corporate system). Also not a duplicate of P6533 ('Columbia Gulf Transmission Pipeline'), which is the system-level mainline row (no segment name, no populated length/diameter/capacity) -- P2556 is a specific, discrete expansion project on that system, the same relationship every other system/project pair on this roster has (e.g., Gulf South's system row vs. its ~9 expansion rows here). Notably, P6533's presence on this same roster, already correctly named 'Columbia Gulf Transmission Pipeline,' independently corroborates that GEM's own data model distinguishes Columbia Gulf from Columbia Gas -- which makes P2556's 'Columbia Gas Transmission' label look like a straightforward data-entry error (see the attribution concern filed below).

validity.researcher_notes: Columbia Gas Transmission, LLC and Columbia Gulf Transmission, LLC are two DISTINCT FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas companies, both historically part of Columbia Pipeline Group and both now subsidiaries of TC Energy -- easy to conflate (as GEM's own sheet appears to have done here) but legally and operationally separate entities with separate FERC dockets, separate tariffs, and non-overlapping (if geographically adjacent/interconnected) pipeline systems. Every independent source found for the Louisiana XPress Project names Columbia GULF, never Columbia Gas: (1) FERC's Certificate Order captions the applicant as 'Columbia Gulf Transmission, LLC,' Docket No. CP19-488-000, and states 'Columbia Gulf is part of Columbia Pipeline Group Inc., which is a subsidiary of TC Energy Corporation' -- Columbia Gas is never mentioned in the order; (2) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset records `pipeline_operator_name = 'Columbia Gulf Transmission'` for this exact project (docket CP19-488) in all 23 releases from July 2019 through August 2026; (3) Natural Gas Intelligence's 2022 article states explicitly: 'TC Energy affiliate Columbia Gulf said it needs until Dec. 31 to construct and make available for service the Shelburn Compressor Station, the final one to be built for the Louisiana XPress Project (LAXP) [CP19-488]'; (4) 1012industryreport.com's trade-press piece on the project also names Columbia Gulf Transmission; (5) TC Energy's own public fact sheet for the project is titled 'About Columbia Gulf Transmission' and states 'TC Energy's Columbia Gulf Transmission stretches 3,368 miles, starting in Kentucky and continuing through Tennessee, Mississippi, and Louisiana' -- immediately followed by the Louisiana XPress Project map and timeline on the same document. Five independent origins (federal regulator's order, federal EIA dataset, two separate trade-press outlets, and the operator's own public materials), zero of which name Columbia Gas Transmission for this project. CAVEAT: on 2023-10-04, TC Energy completed the sale of a 40% non-controlling equity interest in both Columbia Gas AND Columbia Gulf (as a combined package) to Global Infrastructure Partners (TC Energy's own announcement, tcenergy.com/announcements/2023/2023-10-04-...). This sale does not change which entity built/operates the Louisiana XPress Project (TC Energy retains operatorship and the transaction structure sits at a holding-company level above the named FERC-jurisdictional registrant), so Owner1 = 'Columbia Gulf Transmission LLC' at 100% is recommended AS THE DIRECT REGISTRANT, with this 2023 minority-stake sale flagged in case GEM's ownership model wants the indirect GIP interest reflected at a parent level. Not treated as a spec/duplicate issue -- this is a corporate-attribution correction, not a physical-existence or double-count problem.
